subject: Post-call recap: performance & residency constraints for BrightHealth pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@brighthealth.ai>, Kavita Nair <kavita.nair@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: performance & residency constraints for BrightHealth pilot

Hi Oliver / Kavita —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Key requirements you mentioned (please correct if I mis-typed):
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile <= 180ms for short requests (<= 256 tokens) from US and EU users.
- Streaming: client-facing streaming/partial token flush is required for chat flows (ability to stream within 50ms of token generation).
- Throughput / concurrency: sustained 250 concurrent user sessions with ~4 rps per session (target ~1,000 rps peak).
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region; APAC traffic will be routed to APAC data centers with residency for PHI-related requests (BrightHealth will flag PHI payloads).
- Failover: auto-fallback to lower-cost variant acceptable if latency SLO breached, but must not route PHI outside region.

What we will deliver from our side by EOD Thursday:
1) SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (attached) with measured latencies by region using a simulated workload similar to your profile.
2) A proposed routing policy that satisfies the residency gating (region-bound routing + header-based PHI flag).
3) A short ops note on streaming throughput and how we maintain tail latency under continuous batching.

Questions for you / asks:
- Can BrightHealth add a sample of representative payload sizes (typical tokens for prompts & responses) so we can refine the throughput sizing?
- Confirm whether PHI flagging will be performed by your edge (preferred) or needs to be detected by our runtime.

Next steps:
- We’ll run a multi-region synthetic test and share the SLO spreadsheet by Thu COB.
- Proposal: 4-week pilot with US+EU regions enabled; add APAC in week 3 if residency gating tests pass.

Thanks again — I’ll loop in Vivek for the regional routing details.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0174
attachments: SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx
From: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@brighthealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kavita Nair <kavita.nair@brighthealth.ai>, procurement@brighthealth.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 12:52:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance & residency constraints for BrightHealth pilot

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. That looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 180ms p99 target is for text-completion endpoints used in UI (chat) where median is typically 40-60ms. For bulk batch jobs (non-real-time), latency is not critical.
- PHI: our edge will set a header X-BH-PHI=true for requests containing PHI. We cannot allow any PHI payloads to leave the EU for EU-resident patients.
- APAC: we have a small but strategic pilot in Singapore; APAC residency is required for those patients, but for non-PHI traffic APAC->US is acceptable if latencies are much better.
- Throughput: the 1,000 rps peak estimate is accurate for peak marketing events; sustained is closer to 500 rps.

We’ll share a short CSV of sample request/response token sizes by EOD today. Also procurement asked for a short note on where logs are stored and retention policy (we handle that after pilot scoping).

Oliver
Head of Product Integrations | BrightHealth AI

Team — forwarding BrightHealth's clarifications (quoted below). High level asks for our sizing/ops plan:
1) Confirm that we can meet p99 <= 180ms for US/EU for short requests at ~500 sustained rps and 1,000 rps peak while supporting streaming.
2) Confirm routing policy that respects X-BH-PHI header to pin to EU/APAC data planes.
3) Ops note on log retention/location and how it impacts compliance (procurement requested).

Draft tasks:
- Vivek: run a targeted multi-region test (US/EU/APAC) with streaming enabled; capture p50/p95/p99 and include a small heatmap (region_latency_snapshot.png).
- Soojin: write a short doc on header-based residency gating and any edge rules we need for their stack.
- Aditya: sync with procurement on what log retention durations or SOC2 artifacts they will request so we can prepare template language.

Timing: can you turn around the test + drafts by Thu EOD so I can send an internal proposal to Oliver on Fri morning?

Thanks,
M

Marissa / team —

Quick update from early test runs (attached snapshots):
- US -> p50 38ms / p95 85ms / p99 160ms at sustained 500 rps with streaming enabled (batching tuned for 30ms target batching latency).
- EU -> p50 45ms / p95 95ms / p99 170ms under same load when traffic is served from Frankfurt.
- APAC (Singapore) -> p50 55ms / p95 130ms / p99 260ms — APAC p99 breaches 180ms at current config for heavier prompts; we need a smaller model or dedicated APAC capacity to meet the 180ms p99 for those workloads.

Notes:
- Streaming: our runtime can push token deltas within ~25-60ms depending on network and client TCP windowing.
- Residency gating: header-based pinning is straightforward; will return a short playbook for their edge.

Attachments: region_latency_snapshot.png (heatmap), test-config.md (ops snippet)

I recommend we propose a pilot plan: US+EU active, APAC scoped conditionally with dedicated APAC capacity (optional add-on).

-Vivek

All —

This looks solid. Two quick asks before we send to Oliver:
1) Marissa: include a one-page pilot scope with explicit acceptance criteria: p99 <= 180ms (US/EU), streaming enabled, routing respects X-BH-PHI, and logs retained per their requested retention policy (we need the exact number). If APAC is included, mark APAC performance as conditional and quote dedicated capacity.
2) Aditya: please prepare a short commercial note (pilot pricing + optional dedicated APAC add-on) and include any SLA caveats around PHI routing.

Marissa — once the SLO_matrix and heatmap are attached and we have the sample token CSV from BrightHealth, send the proposed one-pager and pilot commercial to Oliver Fri morning.
